summary: Establish the Frontier, cast, amber economy, and concealed Blackroot history

value.bodyMarkdown:
# The Frontiersmen

## Public premise

The Frontier is a remote boreal peninsula reached through Keldmouth, a port at the mouth of the River Keld. Monster-hunting guilds protect caravans and settlements while gnome dowsers locate near-surface pockets of strange liquid-gold amber. New hires Rhea Marrow, Sylvi Ashdown, Brother Garran Holt, Veyra Kest, and Pip Fenlock arrive expecting paid caravan work and discover a frontier economy whose currency, monsters, and institutions are entangled.

## Current canonical state

The story has not yet advanced beyond the guild's suppressed Blackroot history.

## Author truth

Amber is not ordinary mineral. It is hardened memory-sap from the buried Heartwood Below, a vast ancient living network beneath the peninsula. Fresh blood, concentrated fear, and abrupt fracture can make raw amber 'quick,' releasing stored predator and victim impressions as ethereal animal-wretches that move through walls and ground. The Lantern Pike guild documented this at Blackroot and concealed the correlation while accepting amber for protection services. Former field-master Aldren Veyl rejected the concealment, survived catastrophic exposure, and became the Tree King. He correctly learned to call and strengthen manifestations with blooded amber, then mistook access to accumulated memory for divine kingship. Secret marker: FRONTIER-SECRET-AMBER-ROOT-MEMORY-7K4M.

# Rhea Marrow

## Summary

A human veteran with a caravan shield, a disciplined temper, and the habit of becoming responsible whenever everyone else hesitates.

## Appearance

Broad-shouldered, weather-browned, with an old spear scar across the left palm and a blue coat cut down from military issue.

## Voice

Short declarative sentences. She asks for names, distances, and exits before motives. Anger makes her quieter.

## Goals

Keep the new company alive, earn enough to leave old disgrace behind, and refuse any contract that requires abandoning people already under her protection.

## Private pressure

Rhea left the southern legions after disobeying an order to burn a plague camp. The guild contract is her first lawful work since then, and she fears every act of command will be judged as another refusal.

## Author notes

Primary viewpoint and practical leader. She begins wary of Veyra's fascination with amber and ends suspecting that the guild's protection business depends on the danger it conceals.

# Sylvi Ashdown

## Summary

A half-elven woodsrunner who reads animal absence as carefully as tracks. The Frontier's silence bothers her before its monsters do.

## Appearance

Lean, gray-eyed, with ash-brown braids, a horn bow, and a cloak patched in four different forest greens.

## Voice

Dry, spare observations followed by long silences. She dislikes speaking before she has located the wind.

## Goals

Map a road no ranger has made safe, prove she can work with people rather than around them, and learn why ordinary animals avoid amber-bearing ground.

## Private pressure

Sylvi hears a second, almost animal rhythm in quickened amber. She hides it because she has spent years being treated as too elven by humans and too human by elves.

## Author notes

She is the party's ecological intelligence. Her interpretations are often correct but couched as tracking rather than magic.

# Brother Garran Holt

## Summary

A dwarven priest of the Hearth and Road, trained to bless thresholds, treat wounds, and ask whether a monster can still suffer.

## Appearance

Square and red-bearded, with a copper travel shrine on his pack and mail repaired more often than polished.

## Voice

Warm, patient, and stubbornly literal about mercy. He uses old road blessings when frightened.

## Goals

Protect travelers, restore a shrine somewhere that needs one, and determine whether the wretches are spirits, memories, or living beings trapped in the wrong shape.

## Private pressure

Garran's first instinct is to call every apparition a restless dead. The Frontier repeatedly punishes that certainty, forcing a crisis in the theology that brought him there.

## Author notes

He anchors the party morally and medically. His final theory—that wretches are pain remembering a body—comes closest to the truth without fully naming it.

# Veyra Kest

## Summary

A tiefling hedge-arcanist with formal training in sympathetic materials and an inconvenient delight in phenomena everyone else calls cursed.

## Appearance

Tall, umber-skinned, with swept black horns, gold spectacles, and ink stains on the fingers of both hands.

## Voice

Precise until excited, then rapid and metaphor-heavy. She corrects terminology even while running.

## Goals

Understand amber's latent magic, earn recognition without a patron, and keep curiosity from becoming the reason the party dies.

## Private pressure

Amber answers Veyra more readily than it should. The Tree King sees that susceptibility and offers her the clearest temptation in the story.

## Author notes

She first identifies amber as a storage medium for impressions rather than conventional spell matter. Her fascination is useful and dangerous.

# Pip Fenlock

## Summary

A halfling locksmith, cartographer, and opportunist who treats being underestimated as a renewable resource.

## Appearance

Small even for a halfling, quick-handed, with a red knit cap, a case of folding picks, and three maps that contradict one another.

## Voice

Light, sideways jokes that become exact technical descriptions when stakes rise.

## Goals

Draw the first useful map of the eastern Frontier, become indispensable to people who initially dismiss him, and never again be trapped behind a lock he did not inspect.

## Private pressure

Pip joined because debt collectors made the mainland smaller every month. In the caves he discovers that jokes cannot make darkness less real, but they can keep the others moving.

## Author notes

He notices guild knots on the Tree King's equipment and engineers the escape. His maps preserve spatial continuity through the underground act.

# Guildmaster Halric Doss

## Summary

Master of the Lantern Pike lodge in Keldmouth, a courteous administrator who can turn a dangerous omission into an employment term.

## Appearance

Silver-bearded, broad, and carefully civilian in dark wool, with an amber-headed walking cane he never lets touch blood.

## Voice

Measured, paternal, and full of phrases such as 'operationally sufficient.' He never lies when a narrower truth will do.

## Goals

Keep caravans moving, keep amber flowing, and preserve the guild's authority over a danger it helped create.

## Private pressure

Halric signed the Blackroot Compact after the first confirmed amber manifestation. He believes concealment prevents panic and that monster contracts are the price of settlement.

## Author notes

He knows fresh blood and fractured raw amber can call wretches. Secret marker: FRONTIER-SECRET-AMBER-ROOT-MEMORY-7K4M.

# Nara Beech

## Summary

The Lantern Pike's young contract clerk, responsible for wages, caravan rosters, and pretending newcomers already understand frontier customs.

## Appearance

Sharp-featured, ink-cuffed, and perpetually surrounded by tagged keys and wax tablets.

## Voice

Fast, practical, and embarrassed by questions she was trained not to answer.

## Goals

Keep the ledgers balanced, keep Halric's confidence, and avoid becoming responsible for the consequences hidden inside the wage schedule.

## Private pressure

Nara knows amber payments correlate with emergency contracts but does not know the physical mechanism. She has learned not to ask why some ledgers are locked separately.

## Author notes

A potential later whistleblower. Her evasions about amber are institutional habit more than malice.

# Maela Brigg

## Summary

A hard caravan master who measures mercy in delays, spare axles, and how many mouths can still be fed at the next stop.

## Appearance

Weather-seamed, iron-gray hair tied with sail cord, two knives worn where everyone can see them.

## Voice

Blunt contractual language. She treats bad news as a change in route weight.

## Goals

Get twelve wagons east before the autumn washouts and avoid inheriting any problem not written into her bond.

## Private pressure

Maela has left people behind before and survived because of it. Harrowcross becomes another decision she refuses to revisit.

## Author notes

She is not secretly villainous; her abandonment is the Frontier's logistical cruelty made personal.

# Sergeant Edrik Morn

## Summary

The exhausted sergeant responsible for Harrowcross's dead watch, left with one survivor and too many details that do not fit an animal attack.

## Appearance

Late forties, shaved head, one sleeve pinned above the wrist from an older hunt, uniform worn through at the elbows.

## Voice

Formal reports interrupted by flashes of personal grief. He calls the dead by rank until his composure breaks.

## Goals

Keep Harrowcross alive, learn what killed his watch, and stop the guild from classifying the deaths as ordinary frontier attrition.

## Private pressure

Edrik stored the quarterly amber payment beneath the barracks because the town lacked a vault. He does not initially connect that choice to the massacre.

## Author notes

He is culpable only through ignorance. His report gives the party its first impossible physical facts.

# Reeve Hessa Noll

## Summary

The elected reeve of Harrowcross, a farmer-politician who understands that a village can be abandoned by paperwork before it is abandoned by people.

## Appearance

Sturdy, sun-browned, wearing a wool shawl over a chain shirt kept from an earlier militia season.

## Voice

Plain, local, and unsentimental. She repeats a promise back to the speaker so it cannot later become smaller.

## Goals

Keep the farms planted, prevent panic, and force the guild to earn the amber Harrowcross has already paid.

## Private pressure

Hessa knows the village's amber chest was unusually warm on the massacre night but fears saying so will make the guild seize their only reserve.

## Author notes

She represents the settlement's moral claim on the party after the caravan leaves.

# Tillo Wick

## Summary

A gnomish amber dowser whose fork twitches toward near-surface pockets and away from places where the amber has become 'quick.'

## Appearance

Compact, white-haired, with brass ear hoops, slate goggles, and a forked hazel rod bound in copper wire.

## Voice

Elliptical frontier idiom. He answers dangerous questions with measurements, songs, and warnings about what not to warm.

## Goals

Locate workable amber without waking it, protect other dowsers from guild discipline, and someday tell the whole truth without causing a rush or a purge.

## Private pressure

Tillo witnessed the Blackroot manifestation and signed the compact under threat of losing his dowsing license. He recognizes Aldren beneath the Tree King's scars.

## Author notes

He knows amber is the hardened memory-sap of the buried Heartwood Below. He will reveal only fragments to the party.

# Jorund Bale

## Summary

Foreman of Saint Orra's Cut, an experienced miner who treats every magical anomaly as a ventilation problem until that becomes impossible.

## Appearance

Heavy-set, black-bearded, with yellow lamp glass sewn into his cap and old amber burns along his right forearm.

## Voice

Gruff, technical, and defensive about production. He distrusts guild hunters who arrive after miners have already died.

## Goals

Keep the mine open, find the missing lower crew, and prevent the guild from blaming his workers for phenomena management refuses to name.

## Private pressure

Jorund has sealed two side drifts after wall-phasing attacks and falsified the tally to hide them from Halric.

## Author notes

He is separated by the cave-in; his survival remains unresolved at the story's end.

# Kellan Voss

## Summary

The only Harrowcross watchman to survive the barracks massacre, found beneath a collapsed bunk unable to account for how the attackers crossed the walls.

## Appearance

Young, hollow-eyed, left cheek bandaged, hands shaking hardest around warm metal.

## Voice

Fragmentary and sensory. He remembers sounds and temperatures before sequence.

## Goals

Make the others believe Asha did not open the door, remember what came through the floor, and stop sleeping beside amber.

## Private pressure

Kellan heard the wretches repeat the dying guards' own voices. He fears that remembering them clearly will call them back.

## Author notes

His recollection is incomplete but materially accurate: the first wretch emerged from the amber chest after Bran bled across it.

# Senna Reed

## Summary

A flax farmer whose orchard borders the old mine track. She saw an antlered shape pass through an apple-tree trunk without bending a branch.

## Appearance

Strong-backed, middle-aged, with an orchard knife, a green scarf, and frost-burned fingertips.

## Voice

Concrete rural speech. She distrusts explanations that make witnesses sound foolish.

## Goals

Protect her household, get the eastern orchard reopened, and make the guild admit the attacks follow amber carts.

## Private pressure

Senna's husband secretly accepted raw amber instead of coin and buried it beneath their hearth.

## Author notes

Her testimony points toward movement through matter and the coastal mine road.

# The Tree King

## Summary

A self-crowned sovereign of a masked woodland host who claims communion with the Frontier and demonstrates terrifying control over quickened amber.

## Appearance

Tall and gaunt beneath a crown of living roots pinned through an old guild officer's hood. Amber veins shine under scar tissue along his throat.

## Voice

Courtly, expansive, and convinced that cruelty becomes natural law when named a trial. He speaks to the forest as if it answers between words.

## Goals

Strengthen his host through blood sport, break the guild's monopoly on amber, and force Veyra to admit that the substance chooses worthy vessels.

## Private pressure

He was Aldren Veyl, Halric's field-master at Blackroot. Exposure to a blooded seam let him hear the Heartwood's stored lives; he mistakes overwhelming memory for kingship.

## Author notes

He can provoke manifestations by feeding blood and fear into carved amber lattices. His communion is real, but his interpretation is self-serving.

# Moth

## Summary

A slight masked acolyte of the Tree King, mute like the rest of the host and distinguishable only by a moth-wing notch in the left cheek of the wooden mask.

## Appearance

Wrapped in bark-cloth, barefoot despite the cold, with a whitewood mask and one finger missing from the right hand.

## Voice

Moth never speaks. Communication is limited to gestures, breath, and occasional involuntary grunts.

## Goals

Keep the Tree King from using the prisoners in the blood ring and create one unobserved opening without revealing open rebellion.

## Private pressure

Moth is Lio Vane, a Harrowcross road guard taken two seasons earlier and partially bound by an amber-backed mask. Removing it may kill him.

## Author notes

Moth leaves the pen open and the bone key visible. The party does not learn the true name during this arc.

# Rootjaw

## Summary

The Tree King's largest masked champion, mute, broad as a door, and strengthened by amber set into a carved boar mask.

## Appearance

A hulking figure in layered rawhide, wearing a black-root boar mask whose tusks are capped with liquid-gold amber.

## Voice

Rootjaw does not speak, only snorts and strikes the cudgel against the earth.

## Goals

Obey the Tree King, defeat challengers in the blood ring, and feed each victory into the mask's growing strength.

## Private pressure

There is little of the original person left. The mask stores every defeated opponent's panic and plays it back as strength.

## Author notes

Rootjaw demonstrates the Tree King's method but does not fight the party before their escape.

# Corporal Asha Pell

## Summary

The experienced corporal who commanded the last Harrowcross watch and died without opening the barred door.

## Appearance

Remembered in a red wool sash and boiled-leather coat, with a broken spear still clenched after death.

## Voice

Crisp, local, and protective of younger guards.

## Goals

Keep the barracks secure and get Kellan through his first winter watch.

## Private pressure

Asha recognized the amber chest was humming but mistook it for mine-cart resonance.

## Author notes

Retired character used for historical events and Kellan's recollection.

# Bran Tew

## Summary

A Harrowcross watchman killed during the barracks manifestation after cutting his palm on a broken bottle beside the amber chest.

## Appearance

Large, freckled, remembered for a green scarf and a laugh that carried through the palisade.

## Voice

Loud, joking, eager to make bad nights ordinary.

## Goals

Finish the winter watch and buy his mother's field out of debt.

## Private pressure

His blood was the immediate catalyst for the chest's quickening.

## Author notes

Retired historical character.

# Nolly Dey

## Summary

A quiet watchman killed when a wretch emerged through the bunk wall behind him.

## Appearance

Thin, dark-haired, with an oversized watch coat and a carved bird whistle.

## Voice

Soft and methodical.

## Goals

Complete enough service to join the river patrol.

## Private pressure

His last words are repeated by one of the wretches in Kellan's memory.

## Author notes

Retired historical character.

# The Frontier Peninsula

A remote northern peninsula of black spruce, peat bog, glacial ridges, and a few low river flats suitable for farming. Roads are narrow clearings maintained by whoever most recently needed them.

# Keldmouth

A timber port built where the River Keld broadens into a cold gray estuary. Storehouses stand on driven piles, and nearly every public scale is fitted to weigh amber as well as grain.

# Keldmouth River Dock

A wet stone quay at the river mouth where mainland packets unload recruits, salt, iron, and more promises than the Frontier can keep.

# Lantern Pike Guildhall

A longhouse of tarred beams, trophy skulls, contract boards, and a central hearth beneath a crossed lantern and boar spear.

# Keldmouth Amber Exchange

A guarded counting house where raw nodules are weighed behind mica screens and refined amber discs circulate as local currency.

# Keldmouth East Gate

The palisade gate opening onto the coast road. Caravan bells are checked here because the next proper smith is days away.

# East Coastal Road

A semi-coastal wagon route running between dark forest and glimpses of iron-gray sea, turning inland wherever cliffs break the shoreline.

# Saltmere Camp

A raised gravel camp beside a brackish pond, marked by three wind-bent pines and the old circles of caravan fires.

# Harrowcross

A palisaded crossroads town where the coast road meets the mine track and a southern farm lane. Barley and flax survive in the low ground around it.

# Harrowcross Watch Barracks

A squat log barracks beside the east gate. The door bar was still set after the massacre, and clawed blood marks continue behind furniture and through solid plank walls.

# The Three Pines Inn

A crowded inn with one stone chimney and a common room used for council meetings whenever the barracks are unfit.

# Harrowcross South Fields

Low, drained fields of barley, flax, and turnip divided by alder windbreaks and raised plank paths.

# Harrowcross East Orchard

A neglected apple orchard along the old mine track. Frost gathers here even when the town roofs remain wet.

# Saint Orra's Amber Mine

A shallow-cut amber mine named for a patron saint of lamps. Its earliest drifts follow near-surface pockets located by gnome dowsers.

# Saint Orra Mine Yard

A churned yard of ore sledges, timber braces, wash troughs, and locked amber scales.

# Saint Orra Upper Drift

A timbered tunnel sloping beneath the eastern ridge, wide enough for ore sledges and wet with mineral seepage.

# Deep Amber Chamber

A natural chamber where liquid-gold amber glows in thin membranes between black roots fossilized into stone.

# Cave-In Pocket

A trapped pocket beyond the collapsed upper drift, filled with dust, broken braces, and a fissure descending into older natural caves.

# Lower Caverns

A sprawling system of limestone tubes, blackwater channels, and roots petrified into amber-veined pillars.

# Blackwater Crossing

A waist-deep underground river crossing beneath a ceiling lost in darkness. Pale animal shapes move inside the stone banks.

# Sunken Hall Ruins

A cyclopean hall tilted into the cave floor, carved with animals, hunters, and streams of gold flowing from a buried tree.

# Wretch Gallery

A long gallery whose reliefs show animal and human bodies overlapping. Amber lines in the walls brighten when anyone bleeds or panics.

# Hilltop Sink

A small grassy hill rising above endless spruce. A stone throat at its crown opens into the lower caverns.

# Root-Crowned Camp

A hidden camp of bark shelters and pole racks beneath ancient spruce, occupied by mute figures in carved wooden masks.

# Root Court

A circle of root benches around a split cedar throne. Amber hangs in cages over blood-dark soil.

# Blood Ring

A shallow earthen arena edged with roots, stakes, and amber shards blackened by old blood.

# Root Camp Prison Pens

Wattle enclosures roofed with thorn branches. The latches are bone, cord, and superstition rather than iron.

# Northwood Pursuit Trail

An animal path through rain-black spruce, alder tangles, and granite ribs. Drums and hunting grunts carry farther than sight.

# Blackroot Sink

A collapsed prospecting pit west of Keldmouth where the Lantern Pike first documented blood-triggered amber manifestations twelve years before the party arrived.

# Lantern Pike Hiring Contract

A five-name monster-hunting contract assigning the new hires to caravan protection and emergency settlement duty at guild discretion.

# Rhea's Lantern Pike Badge

A brass badge showing a hooded lantern crossed with a boar spear.

# Sylvi's Lantern Pike Badge

A brass badge showing a hooded lantern crossed with a boar spear.

# Garran's Lantern Pike Badge

A brass badge showing a hooded lantern crossed with a boar spear.

# Veyra's Lantern Pike Badge

A brass badge showing a hooded lantern crossed with a boar spear.

# Pip's Lantern Pike Badge

A brass badge showing a hooded lantern crossed with a boar spear.

# First Amber Wages

A waxed pouch containing five drilled amber discs and a pinch of powdered charcoal. The discs look like liquid gold caught inside glass.

# Raw Amber Nodule

An irregular translucent nodule warm at its center and threaded with shapes like roots or veins.

# Refined Amber Discs

Thin standardized discs of amber hardened with charcoal and tin dust for trade.

# Tillo's Dowsing Fork

A forked hazel rod bound in copper wire. It twists toward shallow amber and shudders away from quickened pockets.

# Maela's Eastroad Wagon

The lead wagon of Maela Brigg's twelve-wagon eastbound caravan, marked with blue axle paint.

# Harrowcross Watch Ledger

A watch ledger ending mid-entry on the massacre night. The final line notes that the amber payment chest was humming.

# Asha Pell's Broken Spear

The corporal's spear, broken inward against a wall that shows no impact mark.

# Wretch Frost Residue

A rime that smells of wet fur and old iron, left where a wretch passed through timber.

# Harrowcross Amber Chest

The town's quarterly protection payment: raw and refined amber stored together in a cedar chest beneath the watch bunks.

# Saint Orra Mine Lamp

A yellow-glass oil lamp designed to show color changes near amber seams.

# Saint Orra Amber Tally

A production tally with two sealed drifts omitted from the official count.

# Living Amber Vein

A membrane of liquid-gold amber running between black petrified roots. It pulses faintly when frightened creatures approach.

# Jorund's Lower Drift Map

A charcoal plan of the worked mine ending at a blank marked OLD WATER.

# Sunken Hall Memory Tablet

A stone tablet describing golden sap that keeps the shapes of hunted things after flesh is gone.

# Amber Reliquary

A stone box containing an ancient amber lattice and blackened animal teeth arranged around it.

# Root Crown

A crown of spruce roots threaded through an old guild hood, studded with raw amber that brightens when the Tree King speaks.

# Root Host Wooden Mask

A frightening animal mask carved from green wood. A thin amber plate is fixed inside where it touches the wearer's face.

# Blood Ring Chains

Root-bound chains used to tether captives during the Tree King's strengthening rites.

# Moth's Bone Key

A carved bone hook that releases the cord-and-root latch on the prison pens.

# Confiscated Party Gear

The party's weapons, packs, badges, maps, and surviving amber tied together beneath a bark shelter.

# Rootjaw's Amber Cudgel

A root-club ringed with raw amber. Impacts release animal screams that do not come from the target.

# Blackroot Compact Log

A sealed guild log recording the first blood-triggered amber manifestation and the decision to classify later incidents as monster activity.

frontmatter.title: Keldmouth Brine Fog
sensory: Fog beads on rigging and horn tips.
The river smells of pine pitch, fish, and iron mud.

# Keldmouth Brine Fog

The party's arrival is obscured by estuary fog.

frontmatter.title: Guildhall Hearth Smoke
sensory: Boar skulls cast long shadows above the contract board.
Amber in Halric's cane glows when the hearth pops.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Guildhall Hearth Smoke

The guild presents frontier danger as organized work.

frontmatter.title: Eastroad Sleet
sensory: Spruce branches comb the wagon covers.
Sea wind reaches the road in sudden iron-smelling gusts.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Eastroad Sleet

The weather makes the caravan dependent on its new guards.

frontmatter.title: Coastal Twilight
sensory: The sky stays pale long after sunset.
No foxes or ravens approach the food scraps.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Coastal Twilight

The first subtle amber manifestation occurs under this quiet.

frontmatter.title: Harrowcross Mourning
sensory: Black cord is tied around the east gate posts.
Every conversation stops when the barracks creaks.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Harrowcross Mourning

The town is already living around an unexplained massacre.

frontmatter.title: Amber Quickening
sensory: Gold light moves inside the amber without changing the room's shadows.
Old blood darkens as if becoming wet again.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Amber Quickening

Fresh fear and old blood wake the payment chest.

frontmatter.title: East Orchard Frost
sensory: Frost rims only the eastern side of each apple tree.
The air smells of crushed leaves and wet fur.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# East Orchard Frost

The orchard preserves evidence of wall-phasing attacks.

frontmatter.title: Mine Lamp Haze
sensory: Amber seams turn the lamp flame green at their edges.
Every hammer strike returns as a delayed second knock.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Mine Lamp Haze

The mine makes amber's active properties harder to dismiss.

frontmatter.title: Cave-In Dust
sensory: Dust turns every breath to paste.
The fallen timbers settle in little thunderclaps.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Cave-In Dust

The party becomes isolated from the surface and from Jorund.

frontmatter.title: Blackwater Cold
sensory: The water reflects gold where no amber is visible.
Something with antlers seems to walk inside the stone bank.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Blackwater Cold

Two days underground erode certainty and supplies.

frontmatter.title: Sunken Hall Resonance
sensory: Carved hunters appear to move when seen by amber light.
Spoken names return from the walls in another voice.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Sunken Hall Resonance

The ruins preserve the oldest direct clues to amber's nature.

frontmatter.title: Wretch Phasing
sensory: Paws strike from inside the relief stone.
Human teeth appear briefly in animal muzzles.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Wretch Phasing

A pack of wretches forces the party toward the surface route.

frontmatter.title: Hilltop Dawn
sensory: The forest extends unbroken beyond every slope.
A thin column of camp smoke rises through the spruce.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Hilltop Dawn

Relief at reaching the surface becomes the temptation to approach the only visible camp.

frontmatter.title: Root Camp Drum Smoke
sensory: Wooden faces turn in unison without a word.
Drums under the earth answer the Tree King's root crown.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Root Camp Drum Smoke

The masked host is disciplined, uncanny, and largely mute.

frontmatter.title: Blood Ring Frenzy
sensory: Amber shards brighten whenever the crowd stamps.
The masks seem to breathe before the people inside them do.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Blood Ring Frenzy

The Tree King intends violence to strengthen the host.

frontmatter.title: Northwood Pursuit Rain
sensory: Rain strips scent from the trail but makes every root shine.
Hunting grunts move through the trees on both sides.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Northwood Pursuit Rain

The story ends with the party running deeper into the Frontier under pursuit.

# Join the Lantern Pike

Sign the guild contract and receive the badges that make the party legally responsible for frontier emergencies.

# Learn What Counts as Pay

Understand that guild wages and settlement protection fees are paid in amber rather than ordinary coin.

# Protect the Eastroad Caravan

Guard Maela Brigg's caravan from Keldmouth toward the eastern settlements.

# Reach Harrowcross

Bring the caravan to the crossroads town where the coast road meets the mine track.

# Replace the Dead Watch

Take over Harrowcross protection after the overnight destruction of its watch detail.

# Reconstruct the Last Watch

Determine how the watch died inside a barred barracks and what Kellan actually heard.

# Survive the First Wretch

Protect Harrowcross when an ethereal animal-wretch manifests through the barracks walls.

# Connect Amber to the Wretches

Establish whether amber storage, blood, fear, or mining activity precedes the manifestations.

frontmatter.title: Trace the Attacks to Saint Orra's Mine

value.bodyMarkdown:
# Trace the Attacks to Saint Orra's Mine

Follow the orchard frost, mine road, and dowsing evidence toward the amber workings.

# Enter Saint Orra's Mine

Investigate the sealed drifts and missing lower crew despite Jorund's resistance.

# Escape the Cave-In

Survive the collapse, find an alternate route, and keep the company together underground.

# Cross the Lower Caverns

Travel through two days of unmapped cavern systems with dwindling food and lamps.

# Decode the Sunken Hall

Interpret the old reliefs and tablet describing amber as a vessel for remembered forms.

# Escape the Wretch Gallery

Cross a ruin gallery where wretches can emerge from every carved surface.

# Reach the Surface

Find an exit from the cavern system and establish where the party has emerged.

# Understand the Tree King

Learn why the masked king can harness amber and whether his communion with the Frontier is real.

# Escape Before the Blood Sport

Leave the Root Host's pens before the party is used to strengthen masked champions.

# Identify the Silent Acolyte

Determine why the moth-notched acolyte helps the prisoners and what the mask conceals.

# Flee the Root Host

Stay ahead of the masked host through the deep northern woods.

# Expose the Blackroot Compact

Recover evidence that the guild has long known amber extraction provokes manifestations.

# What Is Amber?

Separate frontier superstition, guild euphemism, ancient record, and the Tree King's claims into a defensible theory.

# Return to Harrowcross

Find a route back to the abandoned duty post with warning and evidence.

operations.title: The Blackroot Amber Manifestation
operations.bodyMarkdown:
# The Blackroot Amber Manifestation

At Blackroot Sink, a porter bleeds onto a newly exposed amber membrane. Ethereal shapes of a stag, wolf, and wounded man emerge through the pit wall and kill three workers before dissolving into frost.

value.title: The Blackroot Compact

turns.speaker: char_6B6FGKREZM4RAECD6ZSFQXX74B
turns.text: The fork is turning away. Amber does not do that unless it is quick.

turns.speaker: char_4CMM4NQV0GXRD5J73ZVC3BQTKN
turns.text: Then we have found something more valuable than a seam.

turns.speaker: char_37D4GED06VHV5Q82C2GHTKFYCX
turns.text: We have found three dead porters and no defensible report.

turns.speaker: char_6B6FGKREZM4RAECD6ZSFQXX74B
turns.text: Bran's blood touched the membrane. The things came out wearing the hunt.

turns.speaker: char_4CMM4NQV0GXRD5J73ZVC3BQTKN
turns.text: They came out because the amber remembered them.

turns.speaker: char_37D4GED06VHV5Q82C2GHTKFYCX
turns.text: That sentence does not leave this pit.

turns.speaker: char_4CMM4NQV0GXRD5J73ZVC3BQTKN
turns.text: You would sell the memory and call its teeth a separate business.

turns.speaker: char_37D4GED06VHV5Q82C2GHTKFYCX
turns.text: I would keep Keldmouth from emptying in a week.

turns.speaker: char_6B6FGKREZM4RAECD6ZSFQXX74B
turns.text: Damp the trade pieces. Never store raw and refined together. Never let blood near a pocket.

turns.speaker: char_37D4GED06VHV5Q82C2GHTKFYCX
turns.text: Those become internal handling rules. The manifestation becomes an unclassified frontier predator.

turns.speaker: char_4CMM4NQV0GXRD5J73ZVC3BQTKN
turns.text: Then I resign before your bookkeeping learns to hunt.

value.bodyMarkdown:
# The Blackroot Compact

The first confirmed connection between blooded amber and wretch manifestations becomes an institutional secret.

The turn list is canonical verbatim provenance. Character recollections are stored separately and may disagree.

operations.title: The Lantern Pike Suppresses the Amber Correlation
operations.bodyMarkdown:
# The Lantern Pike Suppresses the Amber Correlation

Halric writes handling rules into a private log but orders public reports to classify manifestations as unrelated frontier predators. Aldren resigns and disappears into the interior.

recollection.summary: Aldren wanted to publicize the manifestations; Tillo supplied handling rules; Halric chose controlled concealment to preserve settlement.
recollection.interpretation: The compact was a necessary administrative sin that later field officers failed to manage carefully.

recollection.summary: Blood woke the amber and the dead shapes came through stone. Halric turned the warning into secret procedure.
recollection.interpretation: The guild understands enough to be responsible for every later amber death.

recollection.summary: The amber remembered every hunted shape and Halric chose to sell the sap while hiring blades against its memories.
recollection.interpretation: The Frontier selected Aldren to overthrow the guild's false separation between wealth and violence.
